thread:
incident-bot: 🚨 ALERT: Increased routing errors for us-east-1 -> fallback path detected. Error rate > 8% for 5m. Pager paged on-call.
Alice Chen: acked — oncall here, looking now. Which customers? any paging notes?
incident-bot: Affected routes: /v1/generate (hosted), dedicated pools us-east-1a. 2.1k requests failing 5m window. Top error: MISROUTE_TIER_MISMATCH.
Sam Patel: jumping in, running quick query against request logs.
Priya Rao: I see traffic spike from eu-west-1 that was routed to us-east pools — looks like spillover. Sending query results.
Sam Patel: attaching log excerpt:```
[2026-03-15T22:12:01Z] req=abcd1234 route=/v1/generate region=eu-west-1 routed_to=us-east-1 pool=tier-b fallback_model=gpt-small status=200 latency_ms=1200
[2026-03-15T22:12:02Z] req=abcd1235 route=/v1/generate region=eu-west-1 routed_to=us-east-1 pool=tier-a fallback_model=gpt-quant status=500 err=MISROUTE_TIER_MISMATCH
[2026-03-15T22:12:03Z] req=abcd1236 route=/v1/generate region=eu-west-1 routed_to=us-east-1 pool=tier-b fallback_model=gpt-quant status=500 err=MODEL_COMPATIBILITY
```
Nicole Gomez: key observation: routing decision service returned tier-a for some requests even though eu-west-1 should prefer local tier-b until exhaustion. Could be a tiebreak bug in the spillover policy.
James Li: I see a concurrent autoscale event in eu-west-1 that might have caused premature spillover:```
[autoscaler] 2026-03-15T22:11:58Z scale_down start nodes=2->1 reason=cpu_util below threshold
[autoscaler] 2026-03-15T22:12:05Z scale_up start nodes=1->3 reason=queue_depth spike
```
Priya Rao: hypothesis list: 1) autoscaler oscillation caused transient low capacity -> spillover; 2) routing tiebreak favors lower-latency global tier incorrectly; 3) fallback model compatibility check failing causing 500s.
Alice Chen: agreed. Immediate mitigation — can we pause spillover so eu traffic stays queued locally until scale stabilizes?
Sam Patel: we can flip the routing policy for eu-west to strict-local:```bash
# set routing policy to strict-local for eu-west-1 (temporary)
curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN' https://api.redwood.internal/configs/routing -d '{"region":"eu-west-1","policy":"strict-local-temp","ttl":300}'
```
Nicole Gomez: I'm prepping the change now. Will push with deploy-bot.
deploy-bot: :rocket: starting config change: set routing.policy.eu-west-1=strict-local-temp (ttl=300s). Rollout id=rl-20260315-01.
James Li: applying additional mitigation: add model compatibility fallback mapping to avoid gpt-quant selection for tier-a pools. Command:```bash
redwoodctl routing set-fallback-map --from-tier tier-a --avoid-model gpt-quant --force
```
Sam Patel: change applied, I'm watching error rates on the dashboard. Link: https://dash.redwood/internal/incidents/1728004321
Priya Rao: posting quick before/after metrics: error_rate (5m window) us-east-1 -> 8.4% -> 2.2% after policy flip. Latency p95 improved from 1600ms -> 800ms.
Alice Chen: good containment. Customer impact estimate? any premium customers affected?
Nicole Gomez: initial billing logs show ~120 premium requests failed across 6 customers (most retries succeeded). I'll open a customer-impact ticket.
Sam Patel: adding timeline snippet for RCA thread:
- 22:11:58 autoscaler scale_down eu-west-1 started
- 22:12:01 first misroute observed (eu->us routing decision inconsistent)
- 22:12:05 autoscaler scale_up triggered, oscillation in progress
- 22:12:20 mitigation: routing policy strict-local set for eu-west-1 (ttl 300s)
- 22:14:00 error rate returning to baseline

Priya Rao: sharing logs where routing service tiebreak chooses tier-a:```
[router] 2026-03-15T22:12:01Z decision req=abcd1235 candidates=[tier-b, tier-a] scores={tier-b:0.72, tier-a:0.74} policy=spillover tie_break=lower_latency selected=tier-a
```
Nicole Gomez: the tie_breaker favouring lower_latency is expected but we thought strict-local would keep local tier unless exhausted. Need to check the exhaustion detection window.
James Li: looking at code path: spillover logic uses a sliding window of 30s to mark local exhausted. If autoscaler temporarily reduced capacity for >1 request, window logic could prematurely mark exhausted. Potential bug: window uses request rate not in-flight capacity.
Alice Chen: action item: add unit tests for exhaustion detection and change docs. Also add a short-term guard: when autoscaler is active, increase exhaustion threshold.
Sam Patel: creating short post-incident checklist in-thread. Also uploading raw logs to S3: s3://redwood-incident-logs/1728004321/raw-logs.tar.gz
Priya Rao: I'm starting a follow-up RCA doc skeleton and will assign owners.
Nicole Gomez: oncall handoff: I need to go offline in 20m. Alice, can you take next shift and coordinate the RCA?
Alice Chen: yes I'll take it. Alice: handoff notes -> mitigation in place (strict-local ttl 300s), fallback map updated to avoid gpt-quant on tier-a, monitoring alert adjusted to lower sensitivity during autoscale ops.
James Li: tagging next steps: [A] fix exhaustion detection (prio P0), [B] add guard in router for concurrent autoscale events (P1), [C] customer communication for affected premium customers (owner Nicole).
incident-bot: Incident status: mitigated -> observing. Severity: Sev2. Please update the incident channel when RCA doc is available.
Alice Chen: thanks everyone. Leaving final log markers and timeline in the RCA draft. I'll ping for a follow-up async postmortem. :thumbsup:
